name: Citizenship by Naturalisation

requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 15 years of continuous residence in Nigeria.

requirements.blocker_text: Good character, demonstrated integration (language/custom), and intent to be domiciled in Nigeria, to the President's satisfaction.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of means of livelihood and tax clearance
Residence permit and passport bio-data pages
Guarantor documentation (form, photo, CV, ID card)

sources.title: Citizenship and Business Department, Federal Ministry of Interior, Nigeria -- FAQ: Naturalisation requires a minimum of 15 years of continuous residency, good character, proof of integration (language/custom), and a personal application, processed through the Citizenship and Business Department Portal

Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), Chapter III -- Section 27 (Naturalisation): full age/capacity, good character, domicile intent, local community acceptance, and either 15 years continuous residence or 12 months immediately preceding plus 15 years aggregate within the preceding 20 years

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Nigeria). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- the modeled hard requirement (15-year continuous residence) is confirmed at tier-1 directly by candb.interior.gov.ng, Nigeria's own Ministry of Interior Citizenship and Business Department. DISCLOSED BUT NOT MODELED AS A HARD REQUIREMENT: Section 27 of the Constitution (tier-2, via an NGO-hosted verbatim text at citizenshiprightsafrica.org, consistent with this dataset's established convention of treating academic/advocacy hosting of primary legal text as tier-2) also provides an ALTERNATIVE track -- 12 months' continuous residence immediately preceding the application plus 15 years' aggregate residence within the preceding 20 years -- but since this alternative track's specific figures are not independently confirmed at tier-1, it is disclosed here rather than modeled as a second requirement_group, to keep the file's hard requirements cleanly tier-1 and avoid a downgrade to draft over an alternative pathway most applicants won't need anyway (the 15-year-continuous track is the standard route). dual_citizenship_allowed is FALSE for this route specifically: per Section 28 of the Constitution, a person who is NOT a citizen of Nigeria by birth (which includes naturalised citizens) forfeits Nigerian citizenship upon acquiring or retaining another country's citizenship -- this restriction does NOT apply to citizens by birth, who may hold dual citizenship freely, a distinction worth flagging since it means Nigeria's dual-citizenship rules depend on HOW citizenship was acquired, not a blanket national policy either way.
